I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any commentary notes for you yet.

My first attempt to fetch the pages failed because of a bug in my code: it crashed while reading the first result, before saving or showing any content. After that, my tool for reaching the web was cut off for the rest of this turn, so I couldn't retry. I didn't read any page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say. Since I have nothing from any source, I haven't written notes on Psalm 89:1–26 from my own knowledge.

**What I'll do next turn:**
1. **Main sources:** Enduring Word on Psalm 89, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, and Precept Austin's Psalm 89 page.
2. **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible notes, plus Bible Odyssey if it has anything on the Davidic covenant (vv. 3–4, 19–26) or Rahab (v. 10).
3. **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org (in the Latin numbering it is Psalm 88). I'll also check catholic.com and oca.org for v. 26 ("You are my Father") and how Christ is seen in the psalm.
4. **Tradition-specific views:** I'll search for real differences between Protestant traditions, such as whether God's covenant with David has conditions, and for any popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace) on vv. 15–17 and 22–25. I'll only include these where the sites actually discuss them.

Reply "go ahead" and I'll run the research and write the verse-by-verse notes, with a URL for each point.
